Both Juventus and Atalanta will be desperate to get their domestic campaigns back on track when they meet at the Allianz Stadium, with both sides seeking an immediate response after failing to win either of their last two Serie A fixtures.

Match News and Current Form

Juventus enter this clash seeking to stabilise their domestic campaign after a stuttering league run that saw a 1-1 home draw against AC Milan followed by a 3-2 defeat at Sassuolo. Those results briefly triggered media speculation surrounding manager Luciano Spalletti's future, but an injury-depleted Bianconeri side responded emphatically in midweek by crushing NEC Nijmegen 5-0 in the Europa League. Despite recent league hiccups, Juventus boast impressive underlying defensive metrics, having faced the fewest shots (28) and recorded the lowest Expected Goals Against value (1.8) in the division. Those statistics have helped the Allianz Stadium remain a formidable stronghold as Juventus are unbeaten in nine of their last ten competitive home matches (W6, D3).

Atalanta travel to Turin in urgent need of a boost after suffering back-to-back 2-1 defeats against Roma and Cagliari. Maurizio Sarri’s side have experienced an inconsistent start to their league campaign, picking up six points from their opening four matches (W2, L2), with another setback threatening to hand La Dea three consecutive league defeats under the same manager for the first time since April 2025. Defensive vulnerabilities on the road have been a recurring issue, with Atalanta failing to keep a clean sheet in each of their last five away Serie A fixtures stretching back to last season, whilst winning just three of their last 12 competitive away matches across all competitions (D4, L5).

Head-to-Head History

Draws have defined this rivalry since 2017, with 12 of the last 19 Serie A encounters between Juventus and Atalanta ending level. Atalanta have proved particularly resilient in Turin, remaining unbeaten across their last eight away league meetings with Juventus (W2, D6).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Nine of the ten goals in Juventus’ league matches have been scored beyond the hour mark.

Each of Juventus’ last seven home league outings produced exactly two goals.

Atalanta have conceded four of their five league goals after the break.

Seven of Atalanta’s last eight away league matches saw both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

After netting his first competitive goal for Juventus in midweek, Kerim Alajbegović has scored six of his last seven goals inside the first 30 minutes. Including his strike against Cagliari last weekend, Gianluca Scamacca has scored seven of his last ten goals before the break.

Juventus continue to deal with a heavily-depleted squad, with key playmaker Kenan Yıldız and Manuel Locatelli serving as their most significant absences due to long-term injuries. Atalanta are missing only Isak Hien and Kamaldeen Sulemana .

Betting Analysis

Given Juventus’ strong tendency for late action and Atalanta conceding the vast majority of their goals after the break, over 1.5 second-half goals looks to have a very good chance.

Author: Tomáš Vlasák
